Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: All L1 gold-context records report human oral bioavailability values whose central estimates are at or above the 20% threshold, including absolute measurements such as cilomilast 96%, ketanserin 49–60%, and 5-HTP 49%.

Structurally relevant carboxylic-acid and heteroaromatic-acid contexts are positive: moxifloxacin 91%, norfloxacin 22–60% (mean 40%), and cilomilast 96%, indicating that an ionized carboxylic acid does not by itself place F below 20%.
Uracil-dione and fused heteroaromatic contexts also support F ≥ 20%: ketanserin 49–60%, doxifluridine ~50–80% with high systemic availability, and rufinamide 50–85% across formulations.

No L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20%; the only sub-20 values are lower ends of reported ranges (sulpiride 10%, norfloxacin 22%), while their means/central estimates are above threshold.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule itself.
No matched oral-versus-IV exposure data are available for the query; support is analog-based transfer.
Query dose, formulation, and prandial state are unspecified, and bioavailability can be dose/formulation dependent.
The query's low logD (-1.11), high molecular weight (508), and high TPSA (119.85) create permeability uncertainty, but no direct absorption, efflux, or first-pass data are available.
content.decision_summary: All L1 gold-context records uniformly report human oral bioavailability at or above 20% (central estimates ~35–96%), including carboxylic-acid, uracil-dione, and fluorinated aromatic ether analogs relevant to the query. No affirmative evidence supports F < 20%, and the physicochemical prior is mixed rather than definitively low. Therefore, F ≥ 20% is better supported, and the prediction is high with moderate confidence.
